title: Party Drinks
description:
Allow the frozen juices to defrost before mixing. (We like to put the frozen cans in the refrigerator the night before we make the punch.)
Pour all the ingredients together in a big punch bowl. Stir to combine.
Add ice.

If desired, moisten the glasses and dip them in a plate of salt.
The essence of a Margarita is simple (and sometimes simplicity is best): two parts Tequila, one part orange liqueur, and one part lime juice. After that, you can adjust the amounts to your liking.

If you’re wondering about triple sec, which is often listed in recipes for Margaritas: triple sec is an orange liqueur made from the skin of oranges. The word sec is French for dry. Triple comes from the liqueur being distilled three times. It's more refined than Curacao (cure-uh-SOW, rhymes with cow). Curacao is also made from orange peels, but from sour orange peels in Curacao (a place in the Caribbean).
If you’re making the sour mix, combine the lemon juice and sugar, then dilute with water and stir to dissolve the sugar.
Shake with ice and strain into a glass with or without ice.
Or, grind the mixture in a blender with ice to get the desired consistency.
This is a very tasty non-alcoholic drink, but it does mix well with almost all the various “adult” beverages.
This should probably be entitled “Donna’s Party Punch,” since the recipe came from our good buddy Donna Shenk. Thanks Donna!
Again the basics are straightforward: one part whiskey, four parts sour mix, adjusted to your liking.
When we made this for you – in a frozen version, without the whiskey! – we would often add a little frozen orange juice for more flavor and sweetness.
